description: This header file defines an API for managing temporary object directories within a Git repository context. It provides functions to create, manipulate, migrate, and destroy temporary object directories, which are used to handle objects temporarily used during operations like fetches or rebases, ensuring cleanup and correct integration into the main object database.

classes.name: struct tmp_objdir
classes.description: Opaque structure representing a temporary object directory used for staging objects before migrating or discarding.

classes.name: struct repository
classes.description: An opaque structure representing a Git repository; used here as a parameter for creating temporary object directories.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_create
methods.description: Creates a new temporary object directory with a specified prefix, returning NULL on failure.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_env
methods.description: Returns environment variables needed for processes to make use of the temporary object directory.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_migrate
methods.description: Migrates objects from the temporary directory into the main object database and cleans up resources.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_destroy
methods.description: Destroys the temporary object directory, discarding all its objects.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_discard_objects
methods.description: Removes all objects from the temporary directory without destroying the directory itself.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_add_as_alternate
methods.description: Adds the temporary directory as an alternate object store in the current process.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_replace_primary_odb
methods.description: Replaces the primary object database with the temporary directory, optionally destroying it if specified.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_unapply_primary_odb
methods.description: Restores the primary object database if it was replaced, returning the original temporary object directory.

methods.name: tmp_objdir_reapply_primary_odb
methods.description: Reapplies the primary object database, potentially adjusting its path.
